title: A panty liner lasts a day (camera wipe: panty liner → plain black underwear)

format_analysis.format: A faceless brand-voice VO over fast b-roll, opened by a real-hands camera wipe: a panty liner at the lens is swiped away and plain black underwear appears in the same hand. Then the panty liner's daily bin pile (MON→THU), wash/hang/wear, the underwear on a real woman's morning, and an end card to the quiz.
format_analysis.how_it_should_look: Real, bright, morning-light, phone-shot, not glossy. Owned-phone hands at a cream bathroom vanity with natural 1/60s motion blur. The bin plates use the same warm palette (Warm Cream tiles, white bin, pastel wrappers as the only cool colour). The AI woman is graded to match the phone footage: light grain, no beauty glow. Black product is the hero contrast; Claret appears only on the hook pill, the bookend pill and the button. Camera: locked-off tripod for the wipe and the bin (so plates and takes match pixel-for-pixel), with one gentle handheld drift added in the edit; the AI-woman shots feel handheld. Captions: Claret pill for the hook, Plum Ink on a Warm Cream box for kinetic words, Fraunces only for the end-card brand line, all inside the 14–62% safe zone and the 4:5 crop. Sound: a dry-wry light music bed from frame 0 (Meta Sound Collection), an SFX on every cut in the first 10s (achoo, whoosh, peel, clack, crinkle + tick per drop), and a warm, wry female narrator.
format_analysis.runtime_main: 34s (the locked VO at 2.4 words/s runs 34s, not 33s; see vo_fit_issues for the 1s trim)
format_analysis.build_profile: 0–2.5s hook: faceless, hands only, owned-phone, SFX + text, no VO. 2.5–20.8s: faceless VO over hands, bin and product b-roll (owned-phone plus 2 AI bin plates composited in CapCut). 20.8–27.6s: one consistent AI woman (side-on, never speaks) and one AI friend, with VO over. 27.6–34s: owned-phone bookend and an editor end card. Voice: ONE ElevenLabs brand narrator (warm, wry woman in her 30s; US accent per the script), recorded first, with the pictures cut to it. No lip-sync anywhere.

reference_ads.what_we_take: UltraDries video #6. Its rhythm: a new subject or location on nearly every cut, with 8 cuts in 3–10s and a white-box caption mid-frame. We copy the cut density in the bin and wash section (a new angle, day or object every ~1s). We also copy its ease beat ('you wear them, you wash them, you wear them again', 82.6–85.4s), done as our Wash / Hang / Wear-again inserts at one word per picture.

Everdries video #14, 275d. Its frame-0 grammar: the problem object fills the frame with the contrarian line burned in from 0.0s, and a pop lands at ~1s. Then hands handle the pad with in-shot motion (flip, point, unwrap). We copy the object-at-lens hook with an in-hook text pop, and the hands-on inserts (peel, flip, smooth).

Mireva, the Miro #33 example (301d on the Miro card, 321d by our 2026-10-13 pull). It's the camera wipe itself: the product covers the lens at frame 0 and moves away to reveal the scene, all on a real phone, sold to the same 30–45 pelvic-health buyer. We build it as two matched takes joined inside the blur.

recommended.on_screen_timing: 0.0s 'The sneeze-pee plan:' → 0.6s adds 'a sticker.' → slides off with the swipe at 1.0s → 1.4s bridge 'Or… underwear.' → 1.6s adds 'Not a pad, not a diaper.' → out at 2.5s
recommended.style: Claret #A33154 pill with Warm Cream Hanken Grotesk ExtraBold, cap height ~5% of frame height, 2 lines of ≤18 characters, centred, pill top ~18% down, inside the 4:5 crop. The bridge lines switch to Plum Ink on a Warm Cream box in the same spot, so the colour flip marks enemy → us.
recommended.why: It puts the moment and the word 'pee' on screen at 0.0s, so a stranger can't misread it as period care. The panty liner in the hand decodes 'a sticker' instantly. Five words over two pops give a built-in motion event at 0.6s and a tiny open loop ('plan: …?') that the wipe pays off at 1.4s, before the swipe-away point. It's third person with no 'you', so it's Meta-safe. It does the same job as the proven frame 'problem object in close-up + contrarian line burned in' (Everdries 1206351388295667, 275d), in our own words.

alternates.why: One read, with a stance. The whole line lands at 0.0s instead of waiting for a punchline at 0.6s. It keeps 'pee' and the sticker joke, and has no 'you'. This is the strongest challenger: test it first as a text swap with no other production change.
alternates.proven_anchor: "Sneezing shouldn't require crossing your legs." (clinic, 112d; proven on 30–45 women; AD_RESEARCH says it passes the Meta rule as is)

alternates.text: It's 2026. / Why is a sticker still the sneeze-pee plan? 🤢
alternates.why: The exact frame we copy (problem object at lens + date + question), with 'you' swapped for the object, so it questions the panty liner, not her. It's 10 words, so it runs as 2 pops (0.0 / 0.5). V1-a dropped its 'It's 2026' open (it now opens on 'Sneeze. Little pee.'), so this doesn't clash. Drop the 🤢 if it reads as gross-out; the panty liner is clean.
alternates.proven_anchor: "It's 2025! Why are you still using pads? 🤢" (Everdries 1206351388295667, 275d, 6 dupes)

alternates.text: Do NOT buy a panty liner tomorrow. / (Or the day after that.)
alternates.why: Reverse psychology on the enemy object, paid off exactly by the MON→THU pile and 'Tomorrow, a new one.' Weakness: there's no 'pee' or 'sneeze' at 0.0s, so only the achoo carries the topic and a period-care misread is possible. Test it only after the first alternate.
alternates.proven_anchor: "Do NOT buy Everdries tomorrow or the day after that." (Everdries #1 video, 323d)

text_hook.note: The recommended line is the locked script line, wording unchanged. I changed two things. (1) The hook style is now the Claret pill instead of the script's Plum-on-Cream box: a cream box disappears against a cream bathroom wall, and the build rules set the Claret pill as the max-contrast hook. (2) 'Not a pad, not a diaper.' now lands at 1.6s and the hook ends at 2.5s, not 2.2s, so the line is readable for ~0.9s. The first alternate is the one I'd test against it first. Nikita chiefs any wording change.

visual_hook_build.miro: #33 Camera Wipe (in-category proof: Mireva 25242369045401076 and Hoooyi 1648680299903591, 174d). Backup: #61 Object Into Lens.
visual_hook_build.frame_1: A bright cream bathroom vanity in morning sun. A woman's right hand holds one clean, pastel-wrapped panty liner centred ~20cm from the lens, sharp. The Claret pill 'The sneeze-pee plan:' is already on screen ~18% down. The frame is already moving: a 3-frame bump on the achoo plus a slow push. Never dark, never still.
build_steps: Recommendation: owned-phone, filmed the day the samples land. The underwear half needs the real sample either way: no AI product frame can be made until the 5 photos exist, and those photos come from the same samples. So AI doesn't unblock it any earlier. Filming on the phone means zero product drift (the #1 risk on the CJ SKU), real motion blur from a real hand whip (that's what makes a wipe invisible), 0 credits and ~30 minutes. You need a woman's hand model (30s, short natural nails, thin gold band) and a bathroom with a window.

SET: bathroom vanity, window camera-left at ~45° to the lens, overhead lights OFF (no mixed colour). Behind: a Warm Cream or white wall, the basin edge low in frame, the toothbrush cup on the right third. Tape marks on the counter for the cup and soap so nothing moves between takes. Angle the mirror so it doesn't show the phone or a person.

CAMERA MATCH: phone on a tripod, vertical, NEVER touched between takes. Main 1x lens. Turn auto-macro OFF (it switches lenses at 20cm and the field of view jumps), and turn portrait/cinematic mode OFF (fake blur tears around moving hands). Lens height = hand height (~30cm above the counter), level, 0° tilt. In the Blackmagic Camera app: 4K 30fps, shutter 1/60s for natural whip blur, WB 5600K, and ISO, focus and exposure locked at 20cm.

HAND MATCH: always the right hand, same grip (thumb in front, fingers behind), same wrist angle, same sleeve (bare forearm), same ring. A 20cm string tied to the tripod puts the hand at exactly 20cm; a resting block out of frame makes it repeatable. Centre the object on the phone grid, top of the object at ~35% down, clear of the text zone (14–30%).

LIGHT + BACKGROUND MATCH: shoot take A and take B back-to-back within 5 minutes, so daylight can't shift. If clouds are moving, use one LED panel at a fixed spot instead of the window. The background is identical: nothing on the counter moves.
TAKE A (panty liner, 8–10 takes): hold ~2s with tiny natural drift, then on the cue whip left→right across and past the lens, close enough that the wrapper fills the frame, and exit right.

TAKE B (underwear, 8–10 takes): start with both hands out of frame-left, whip in left→right at the SAME speed and distance, stop dead on the mark holding the underwear stretched by its waistband, hold ~2s, then a small stretch-release snap. The motion direction continues from take A, so the vectors match. Same session, also film: B2 (the same whip-in, then a slow half-turn to the back, for S12), a fresh panty liner held then whipped out (for S11), and the underwear held still with a small stretch (the bookend, S18).

JOIN in CapCut: copy one grade onto both takes. Align the blur peaks and cut on the frame where the blur covers ≥80% of the frame on both (~1.2s). Add 2–4 frames of horizontal directional blur across the join, plus a whoosh. Nest S1+S2 as one compound clip and add ONE gentle handheld drift (Shake 'low') over the whole thing, so the movement runs continuously across the join. Add the 3-frame bump at 0.0 on the achoo.

TEXT: Claret pill 'The sneeze-pee plan:' at 0.0. 'a sticker.' pops at 0.6 (scale 90→100% over 4 frames). The pill slides off right with the swipe at 1.0. 'Or… underwear.' lands at 1.4 and 'Not a pad, not a diaper.' at 1.6, Plum Ink on Warm Cream.

QC: scrub the join frame by frame at 100% on a phone screen. If the cup or basin edge jumps, nudge take B's position or scale by up to ±2% to match take A. This only works if the phone never moved; if it did, reshoot.
visual_hook_build.lane_and_tool: RECOMMENDED: owned-phone (2 matched locked-off takes on a tripod, Blackmagic Camera app, joined inside the blur in CapCut): 0 credits, real product, real physics. FALLBACK: AI start frames. Use only if no woman's hand is available, or to cut a timing animatic before the samples land.
visual_hook_build.fallback: AI frame pair: Nano Banana Pro frame A (hand + pastel panty liner at the vanity, 9:16, 2k). Frame B is an EDIT of frame A, not a fresh generation: use frame A as the input and swap the panty liner for the underwear, using the 5 reference photos as product references. That keeps the background, light and hand pixel-identical. Then either (a) move it in the editor only: push-in, shake, keyframed whip with directional blur (0 video gens, recommended), or (b) run each through Kling 2.x from a start frame, 5s, 'the hand holds still then whips right out of frame' (2–4 gens), rejecting any hand or product drift. No product frame is ever generated from text alone. Before the photos exist: cut the animatic with take A only and a grey placeholder for B.
failure_modes_to_reject: Background jumps at the join (cup, basin edge or wall line moves): the phone moved, so reshoot
Light or white balance differs between halves (B cooler or darker): daylight shifted, so reshoot inside 5 min or use a lamp
Hand jumps in size, position or wrist angle; different ring or sleeve
Whip too slow (>0.4s), so two clips show; or whip directions don't match (A exits right, B must enter from the left)
Auto-macro lens switch or focus breathing mid-take (field of view jumps)
Any brand print on the panty liner wrapper or release strip (Always / Carefree / Poise look-alikes), any stain or yellow tint
Underwear that isn't the real CJ pair: lace, logo, wrong rise or waistband, gusset or seams not on the sample (AI fallback)
AI hand artefacts: extra or fused fingers, plastic skin, fabric melting into fingers
Hook text sitting over the wipe edge and unreadable, or not cleared by the swipe

vo_fit_issues: RUNTIME: the locked VO is 69 spoken words = 28.8s at 2.4 w/s. Starting at 2.5s, with the pile's staccato pauses and a 1s music breath in the getting-dressed beat, the main cut lands at 34.0s, not the script's ~33s. Proposed trim to get back to ~33s: see the next line.

Beat 5 (13.7–20.8): 17 words = 7.1s in a 7.1s window, zero slack. The word swap makes it worse: 'Plain black underwear' → 'Plain black underwear' adds ~0.3s and creates an underwear/underwear echo ('Or… there's underwear. Plain black underwear.'). PROPOSED TRIM (Nikita OKs): 'Or… plain black underwear.' (−2 words, −0.9s). That brings the main cut to ~33s.

Beat 4 pile (6.3–13.7): 17 words = 7.1s in 7.4s. It fits only at a brisk staccato read (ElevenLabs speed ~1.05). If the read comes in slower, let 'Tomorrow, a new one.' overlap the whip into S12 rather than cut a word.
'Worn again — not binned.' (4 words, 1.7s) runs ~0.2s past S17 into F1. That's fine as an L-cut, because the next VO line starts at 21.0.

Hook: VO-free 0–2.5s by design (the hook lives in SFX + text). Both primary refs talk from frame 0 (UltraDries #6 and Everdries #14), and V1-a talks from 0.1s. I recommend testing a variant where the narrator reads the burned-in hook from 0.3s ('The sneeze-pee plan… a sticker. Or… underwear.', 6 words in 2.2s, which fits). It adds no time and makes sound-on viewers get words, not just music, in the first 2.5s. See open_for_nikita.
Script timing shift: the VO starts at 2.5s instead of 2.2s, so 'Not a pad, not a diaper.' gets ~0.9s on screen in the hook.
pacing_check.notes: Compared with the refs: UltraDries #6 averages 2.6s per shot with 8 cuts in 3–10s. This board averages 1.4s with 6 hard cuts in 3–10s, plus a wrapper drop, tag flip or kinetic word inside every bin shot, so the picture changes every ~0.5s. The bin section alternates plate A (3/4) and plate B (top-down) at 100 → 115 → 100 → 130 → 130 → 100% plus a day→evening grade, so the same plate never sits unchanged for more than 1.1s. The hook is one continuous 2.5s move with its cut hidden in the wipe blur, like every top ref (none hard-cut in 0–3s). Nothing sits still for more than 1.8s except the moving product hold (S12, 2.5s) and the end card (5.0s). The 18–27s section changes room 3 times (bedroom → hallway → front door → street) and angle on every shot (side profile → ECU → low wide → over-the-shoulder → low 3/4 tracking). The day clock carries on past the script's 4 drops: Thursday night's lid-slam, then FRI on a fresh panty liner, which sets up the second wipe for free. Optional for sound-off viewers: burn the VO as small captions over S3–S5, which the script leaves clean. LONG CUT (~55s): add the script's ~5s product beat after the hook, extend the pile to MON→SAT with 'Still a fresh one tomorrow.', hold the getting-dressed section longer and add one more everyday movement (reach or bend). Same end card.

compliance_flags: ALIVE MOMENT vs HARD RULE: the script's beat 6 offers 'a real, easy laugh with a friend over coffee'. The build rules ban any sneeze/jump/laugh performed AFTER the product appears, because a laugh straight after the underwear reads as a performance claim. I boarded the script's other option instead: a warm smile, a coffee handoff with a friend and walking off together (F5). No laugh, no leak acted, no children. Nikita confirms (script Q6).

AI disclosure: a small 'AI-generated' tag on every AI-woman shot (F1–F5), plus the caption line, C2PA/IPTC kept on export and the Ads Manager AI toggle. The bin plates are AI objects and are covered by the caption line. If the woman is ever filmed for real, drop the tag.
Body framing (F1): strictly side-on, waist-to-knee, the top covering the hip, the underwear visible only on the side of the thigh for ~0.5s. Reject any take framed on the butt or crotch.
Wash shot (S13): a plain drum, NO mesh wash bag. The Wash Bag is a bundle gift, and gifts don't go on screen.
Panty liners: plain unbranded wrappers AND release strips (many strips are printed with the brand). Clean white, no stains, no yellow tint, no look-alike brand marks.
Kinetic text 'Feels like a diaper.' sits over a bin of wrappers, so it reads as how the panty liner feels (form), never next to a performance verb. That keeps it inside the CJ column (script Q4).
'hold' appears only inside the guarantee line ('30 nights to see if they hold'). 'leak-resistant' and 'for the sneeze, the laugh and the jump' appear nowhere (wear-test gate).
Day tags and 'Not a pad, not a diaper.' were moved from the script's 'lower third' up to ~56% down, so they stay inside the 14–62% safe zone, clear of the Reels/Feed UI.

Launch gate from the script still stands (Q3/Q7): try.leapproof.com/match must resolve, and the landing must be clean (fake reviews removed, guarantee terms + AI disclosure live, pixel in) before V1-c gets spend.
